content.english: But wisdom, where shall it be found?
And where is the place of understanding? (Job 28:12)
Humanity knows not the price thereof;
neither is it found in the land of the living. (Job 28:13)
The deep says: ‘It is not in me’;
and the sea says: ‘It is not with me.’ (Job 28:14)
It cannot be gotten for gold,
neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof. (Job 28:15)
It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir,
with the precious onyx, or the sapphire. (Job 28:16)
Gold and glass cannot equal it;
either shall the exchange thereof be vessels of fine gold. (Job 28:17)
No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal;
yea, the price of wisdom is above rubies. (Job 28:18)
The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it,
either shall it be valued with pure gold. (Job 28:19)
From where, then does wisdom come?
And where is the place of understanding? (Job 28:20)
Seeing that is hid from the eyes of all living,
and kept close from the birds of the air. (Job 28:21)
Destruction and Death say:
‘We have heard a rumor thereof with our ears.’ (Job 28:22)
God understands the its way,
and He knows its the place. (Job 28:23)
For He looks to the ends of the earth,
and sees under the whole heaven; (Job 28:24)
When He makes a weight for the wind,
and metes out the waters by measure. (Job 28:25)
When He made a decree for the rain,
and a way for the storm of thunders; (Job 28:26)
Then did He see it, and declare it;
He established it, yea, and searched it out. (Job 28:27)

content.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר ׀ לָאָדָ֗ם הֵ֤ן יִרְאַ֣ת אֲ֭דֹנָי הִ֣יא חׇכְמָ֑ה
content.transliteration: Vayyomer la’adam, hen yir’at adonai hi ḥochma,
content.english: And unto humanity He said: ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom;
and to depart from evil is understanding.’ (Job 28:28)

content.hebrew: רֵ֘אשִׁ֤ית חׇכְמָ֨ה ׀ יִרְאַ֬ת יְהֹוָ֗ה שֵׂ֣כֶל ט֭וֹב לְכׇל־עֹֽשֵׂיהֶ֑ם
content.transliteration: Reshit ḥochma yir’at adonai, sechel tov lechol ‘osehem,
content.english: The fear of Adonai is the beginning of wisdom; all those that do them have a good understanding;
His praise endures for ever. (Psalms 111:10)

introduction:
Introduction

Name: והחכמה מאין תמצא, Vehaḥochma Me’ayin Timmatsē

Introduction:

This text is taken from Job 28:12–28, followed by Psalms 111:10. The Job passage is a hymn in praise of Wisdom; because Jewish tradition understands “Wisdom” throughout Job and Proverbs to refer to the Torah, this means that the Job passage is understood as a hymn in praise of the Torah. Thus, it is appropriate to read on Shabbat Bereshit, before we start to read of the whole Torah from the beginning, as well as on the weeks when we read the Ten Commandments, which were the occasion par excellence of divine revelation of Torah. The one line from Psalms, recited after the Job passage, also speaks of wisdom, and thus is an appropriate conclusion to the passage.

Name: והחכמה מאין תמצא, Vehaḥochma Me’ayin Timmatsē

Category: Liturgy

Sub-Category: Biblical verses

Genre: Introduction to Torah-reading

Occasion: Shabbat Bereshit, Shabbat Yitro, Shabbat Va’etḥannan

Composer: N/A (Biblical Verses)

Liturgical Slot: Before the beginning of the parasha (Shabbat Bereshit); in the middle of the parasha, before the reading of the Ten Commandments (Shabbat Yitro, Shabbat Va’etḥannan)

Source: Vilna Siddur, Volume 1, page 407

Cantorial Notes: The individual reciting this passage traditionally reads the opening part of each sentence, and the congregation responds with the closing portions. The congregation’s response begins with each asterisk.
